Arya: quick sync — experiment results for fair-share ramping are in, small sample but noisy
Sam: cool, what metric are we looking at?
Arya: p50 latency, p95 latency, and batch fill rate per tenant during ramp windows
Lee: fill rate dropped ~18% when we increased ramp aggressiveness, p95 spiked ~120ms
Pat: ouch. was that correlated with eviction churn?
Arya: yes, eviction count went up roughly 2x in the same window
Nina: hypothesis: when ramping faster we admit more small requests that never coalesce, causing more early evictions
Sam: can we gate ramp on observed batch occupancy instead of raw inflight?
Lee: yeah, occupancy signal would avoid admitting if current cohort is thin
Pat: implementation-wise that's a prefetch vs admit decision: prefetch still warms KV cache but doesn't count towards admission credits
Arya: draft idea: two-phase admission: reserve a tentative slot (cheap) then confirm when occupancy threshold met; if not, cancel reservation after short timeout
Sam: should we count tentative reservations toward tenant fairness? might be exploited
Nina: make tentative reservations weightless for fairness accounting, but track them to avoid unbounded churn
Lee: eviction timing matters too — if evict cooldown is too short we thrash; need hysteresis on evictees
Pat: propose: backoff per-tenant eviction penalty that increases for repeated evicts within Xs
Arya: that would penalize noisy tenants but could starve legitimate bursts — need escape hatch for SLO-critical requests
Sam: add a bypass flag for high-priority routes (route-level QoS) and charge stricter accounting for them
Nina: telemetry: we need three new metrics: tentative_reservations, confirm_rate, and eviction_backoff_weight per-tenant
Lee: agree. also add sample traces linking reservation -> batch_id -> eviction events, helps root cause
Pat: what about cost? tentative reservations increase memory/KV working set temporarily
Arya: keep tentative window short (10–30ms) and limit per-tenant concurrent tentative slots to small N
Sam: if tentative window too short we might cancel useful joins on slow clients — tradeoff
Nina: can we use client RTT hint or sequence-length prediction to adapt tentative timeout? (e.g., long-seq likely to coalesce)
Lee: that gets complex but doable; maybe start simple with static timeout + telemetry to iterate
Pat: rollout plan: feature-flag two-phase admission, default off. Run on a handful of low-risk shards for 2 weeks
Arya: experiment plan: A/B — baseline vs two-phase. Track p50/p95 latency, fill-rate, evictions, cost delta. Success if p95 improves or fill-rate increases without >5% cost bump
Sam: rollback conditions: spike in p50>100ms or eviction rate >1.5x baseline for 5m
Nina: I'll add the metric dashboards and alerts for those rollback triggers
deploy-bot: deploy queued: canary to s-12 with feature-flag two_phase_admit=false
Arya: thanks — I'll open a follow-up RFC with the admission state machine sketch and pseudo-code
Sam: +1, include a short section on fairness accounting implications
Lee: also include a section on long-term: move from tentative -> informed admission using learned sequence profiles
Pat: cool. ping me when RFC is up, I'll review the telemetry and rollout checklist
Nina: tagging infra oncall in thread for capacity considerations @infra-oncall :eyes:
Arya: noted, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
